prompt: A startup needs three virtual machines, a PostgreSQL database and a bucket for images. A colleague says DigitalOcean is a toy and only AWS is serious. What is wrong with the argument?
hint: List what the design needs and check it against the short list.

choices.text: Everything this design needs is in the core both kinds sell
choices.why: Right. The difference would be the bill's shape and what the team runs itself, not seriousness.

choices.text: Nothing: small providers lack PostgreSQL
choices.why: PostgreSQL runs on any virtual machine, and DigitalOcean also sells it managed.

choices.text: AWS is more expensive, so for a team this small it is always the wrong choice
choices.why: That swaps one ladder for another. Price is one question of several, and not the first.

choices.text: Object storage exists only at the hyperscalers
choices.why: DigitalOcean sells Spaces, an S3-compatible object store. Object storage is part of the core.

prompt: Your design needs a message queue, and you pick a provider that sells only the short list. What does that choice leave you?
hint: Who patches the queue and who wakes up at night?

choices.text: A worse queue, since the provider's machines are slower
choices.why: A virtual machine is a virtual machine. The queue software is the same program wherever it runs.

choices.text: A redesign: without a managed queue the application has to drop it
choices.why: Nothing forces that. You run the queue yourself, on a machine you rent.

choices.text: Installing and operating the queue yourself on a virtual machine
choices.why: Right. Patching, replication and the night call become yours, which is what the lower bill pays for.

choices.text: Nothing extra: every provider sells a managed queue now
choices.why: Managed queues are among the services that stay at the hyperscalers.

prompt: Which of these are part of the core that both hyperscalers and smaller providers sell? Choose all that apply.
hint: The short list, not the long one.

choices.text: Virtual machines
choices.why: The first item on every provider's list.

choices.text: A managed data warehouse
choices.why: BigQuery and Redshift are hyperscaler products; the short list has nothing like them.

choices.text: Load balancers
choices.why: DigitalOcean, Hetzner and Akamai all sell one; Akamai calls it a NodeBalancer.

choices.text: Object storage
choices.why: Spaces, Hetzner Object Storage and Akamai Object Storage, all S3-compatible.

choices.text: A managed machine-learning platform
choices.why: One of the hundreds of services around the core, sold by the three.

prompt: Why do DigitalOcean Spaces and Cloudflare R2 describe themselves as S3-compatible?
hint: Think of a program written against S3.

choices.text: They run on Amazon's hardware, under a licence that Amazon grants them
choices.why: They run in their own data centres. Compatibility is about the API, not the machines.

choices.text: They answer the API that S3 defined
choices.why: Right. A program written for S3 talks to them by changing an address and a key.

choices.text: It is a legal requirement for anything sold as object storage
choices.why: No law asks for it. It is a commercial choice that makes switching easy.

choices.text: They store files in exactly the same price tiers that S3 uses
choices.why: Prices differ; R2, for one, charges nothing for data leaving it.

prompt: A colleague created an EC2 machine yesterday. Today, signed in to the same account, she sees no machines at all in the console. What is the likeliest explanation?
hint: The console shows one of something at a time.

choices.text: The machine was deleted overnight by AWS
choices.why: Nothing is deleted by the provider for sitting idle. Check where you are looking first.

choices.text: Her permissions were removed
choices.why: Then she would see an access error rather than an empty list.

choices.text: A different account is billing the machine
choices.why: The account is the same by the question's own terms; the machine lives in it.

choices.text: The console is showing another region
choices.why: Right. A machine exists only in its region, and the console shows one region at a time.

prompt: Your whole system runs in sa-east-1, and you put CloudFront in front of it with your own TLS certificate. In which region do you request the certificate?
hint: The oldest region has a special role.

choices.text: sa-east-1, beside the rest of the system
choices.why: That is the natural guess, and it is exactly the surprise: CloudFront reads it from elsewhere.

choices.text: us-east-1, always, whatever region the rest is in
choices.why: Right. Some global services are managed from us-east-1, and CloudFront certificates are one.

choices.text: Any region, since certificates are global
choices.why: A certificate in AWS is a regional resource; CloudFront looks in one region only.

choices.text: None: CloudFront refuses your own certificates
choices.why: It accepts them; the rule is only about where they are requested.

prompt: A company's staff already sign in to e-mail and documents through Microsoft 365. What is Azure's strongest argument to this company?
hint: Who is signing in, and where does that list live?

choices.text: Azure runs only Windows, which the staff already know how to use
choices.why: Azure sells Linux machines as a matter of course. The argument is elsewhere.

choices.text: Its access control uses the directory they already sign in with
choices.why: Right. One account for e-mail and cloud, and disabling a leaver closes both.

choices.text: Microsoft 365 customers pay no separate bill for their Azure machines
choices.why: The two are billed separately. What is shared is the directory.

choices.text: Azure is the only cloud with a region in Brazil
choices.why: AWS and Google Cloud have São Paulo regions too.

prompt: An engineer cleans up by deleting the resource group test-shop. Weeks earlier somebody had put the production database in that group. What happens to the database?
hint: What does a resource group hold, and what does deleting it do?

choices.text: Azure refuses, because the group holds a database
choices.why: No such rule exists by default; the group is deleted with its contents.

choices.text: It moves to the subscription's default group
choices.why: There is no default group to catch it. Every resource belongs to exactly one group.

choices.text: It is deleted with every other resource in the group
choices.why: Right. That is what the group is for, and why putting a resource in the wrong one is dangerous.

choices.text: Nothing: resource groups are only labels for billing
choices.why: Billing attaches to the subscription. A resource group is a container whose deletion deletes.

prompt: Put Azure's boxes in order, from the widest to the narrowest.
hint: The directory holds everything; a single VM holds nothing.
trap: Subscription and resource group swapped is the usual slip: the bill attaches to the subscription, and resource groups sit inside it.

prompt: Microsoft's directory of people and groups, called Azure Active Directory until 2023, is now called ___ ID.
hint: A word that starts with E.

prompt: At Google Cloud, what does every resource have to belong to?
hint: It has an id you choose once.

choices.text: A project
choices.why: Right. A project is linked to a billing account, and its id cannot be changed.

choices.text: A resource group
choices.why: That is Azure's box.

choices.text: A folder under the organisation
choices.why: Folders are optional and group projects; resources sit in projects.

choices.text: A region's own account
choices.why: No provider in this lesson makes you open an account per region.

prompt: One VM runs in southamerica-east1 and another in europe-west1, both in the same Google Cloud VPC network. What is true?
hint: Where does a Google VPC network belong, and where do its subnets?

choices.text: They cannot share a network, because each network belongs to one region only
choices.why: That is true of AWS VPCs and Azure virtual networks, not of Google's.

choices.text: One private network, through regional subnets; firewall rules still apply
choices.why: Right. The network is global, the subnets regional, and no joining of two networks is needed.

choices.text: The global network makes the round trip as short as within one region
choices.why: The packet still crosses an ocean. What disappears is plumbing, not distance.

choices.text: They talk only over the internet, by public address
choices.why: They reach each other by private address inside the one network.

prompt: What does the sentence "Kubernetes came out of Google" mean?
hint: Think of Borg and of 2014.

choices.text: Kubernetes runs only on Google Cloud, and the others license a copy
choices.why: All three hyperscalers, DigitalOcean and Akamai sell managed Kubernetes.

choices.text: Google still owns it and charges the other providers to run it
choices.why: It was released as open source; nobody pays Google to run it.

choices.text: Google designed it, after Borg, and released it as open source
choices.why: Right. GKE, Google's managed version, came early, and the project itself belongs to no provider.

choices.text: It is Google's own name for the service that rents virtual machines
choices.why: That is Compute Engine. Kubernetes places containers on machines.

prompt: Match each question to the box that answers it.
hint: Two answers belong to Azure.

pairs.left: Where must every AWS resource sit?
Where must every Azure resource sit?
Where does Azure attach the bill?
Where must every Google Cloud resource sit?

prompt: How does DigitalOcean charge for a Droplet?
hint: One price per size, and a ceiling.

choices.text: A monthly price per size; the time it exists is charged up to that price
choices.why: Right, with a pooled allowance of outbound transfer included.

choices.text: Per request, like functions
choices.why: That is the serverless model of lesson 8, not a virtual machine's.

choices.text: By the second, with the disk, the address and the transfer each metered apart on lines of their own
choices.why: That is the hyperscaler shape. A Droplet's size includes disk and address.

choices.text: A yearly contract paid in advance
choices.why: No contract is needed; a Droplet is charged for the time it exists.

prompt: A small project's AWS bill has four lines for one machine: instance hours, an EBS volume, a public IPv4 address and data out. Moved to a Droplet, which of them become part of the Droplet's price?
hint: Look at the comparison table in the section.

choices.text: Only the instance hours; everything else stays a separate line
choices.why: The Droplet's size also carries its disk and its address.

choices.text: All four, with no limit at all on how much data goes out
choices.why: Transfer is included up to an allowance; beyond it, it is charged per GB.

choices.text: The hours and the disk, never the address
choices.why: A Droplet reaches the internet with a public address included in its price.

choices.text: All four, with data out included up to an allowance
choices.why: Right. Machine, disk and address are in the size; transfer is in, up to the pooled allowance.

prompt: The sheet prices a public IPv4 address at 0.0050 USD an hour in both regions. What does one address cost for a 730-hour month?
hint: Hourly price times hours.

prompt: What separates a Hetzner dedicated server from a Hetzner Cloud server?
hint: One of them is a physical machine.

choices.text: The dedicated server is a whole physical machine, rented by the month and not created by an API call
choices.why: Right. Minutes to hours to arrive, and bought for a load you already know.

choices.text: The cloud server is faster because it is newer
choices.why: Speed depends on the hardware, not on the product line.

choices.text: Only the dedicated server runs Linux
choices.why: Both run Linux; the difference is physical versus virtual.

choices.text: The cloud server includes a managed database
choices.why: Hetzner's catalogue is the IaaS layer: the database is yours to run either way.

prompt: Hetzner's list prices sit well below the hyperscalers' for the same processors and memory. What does that tell you about the machine?
hint: Where does the difference come from?

choices.text: It is oversold, so it is slower
choices.why: Nothing in the lesson supports that; the difference comes from what surrounds the machine.

choices.text: Nothing: it comes with less around it, not a weaker machine
choices.why: Right. A short catalogue and its own data centres explain the price.

choices.text: It lacks a public address
choices.why: Cloud servers reach the internet like any other.

choices.text: It is a trial that expires
choices.why: It is an ordinary product, billed by the hour up to a monthly cap.

prompt: A physical machine rented by the month, with nobody else running on it, is called a ___ server.
hint: It is yours alone, down to the hardware.

prompt: Who owns Linode today?
hint: A content delivery network.

choices.text: DigitalOcean, since a merger of the two companies
choices.why: The two were competitors and still are.

choices.text: Cloudflare, which runs it at the edge
choices.why: Cloudflare does not rent virtual machines at all.

choices.text: Akamai, which bought it in 2022
choices.why: Right. The name Linode survives in the API, the CLI and the documentation.

choices.text: Nobody: it closed down in 2022
choices.why: It was bought and is still sold, now under Akamai's name.

prompt: What is the argument for Akamai's cloud that DigitalOcean and Hetzner cannot make?
hint: What did Akamai already own before 2022?

choices.text: VMs next to a delivery network that reaches past its regions
choices.why: Right. Build in a region, deliver through the edge, one company and one bill.

choices.text: The lowest prices in the market, well below DigitalOcean and Hetzner
choices.why: The course captured no Akamai prices, and price is not its distinctive claim.

choices.text: Hundreds of managed services, as many as the hyperscalers sell
choices.why: Its list is the short one, with names of its own.

choices.text: It is the oldest cloud, older than any of the hyperscalers
choices.why: Linode is older than EC2, but that is not what Akamai sells it on.

prompt: A team wants to rent a virtual machine from Cloudflare for its database. What should they know?
hint: Cloudflare sits in front of servers.

choices.text: Cloudflare's virtual machines come with no disk attached
choices.why: There are no Cloudflare VMs to have one.

choices.text: It rents none; it runs code and storage on its edge network
choices.why: Right. Workers, R2 and small databases, and lesson 8 is where they are covered.

choices.text: They have to buy them through Akamai instead
choices.why: Akamai is a different company with its own cloud.

choices.text: Only in the São Paulo region, where Cloudflare keeps its machines
choices.why: Cloudflare has no regions of virtual machines at all.

prompt: What is OVHcloud's main argument to European buyers?
hint: Whose law applies?

choices.text: It is the only provider with data centres in Europe
choices.why: All three hyperscalers and Hetzner have them. The argument is who owns the company.

choices.text: It sells more managed services than AWS does
choices.why: Its list is growing, but breadth is AWS's argument, not OVHcloud's.

choices.text: Jurisdiction: European law, not American
choices.why: Right. The hyperscalers are American companies, subject to American law wherever their buildings are.

choices.text: It bills in reais, which avoids the exchange rate
choices.why: That is the argument of a Brazilian provider such as Magalu Cloud.

prompt: Match each provider to the reason a customer meets it.
hint: Ask what each one exists for.

pairs.right: The company already runs Oracle Database
OpenShift, from Red Hat, in the office and in the cloud
A Brazilian company, billing in reais

right_distractors: Renting virtual machines at the edge

prompt: Match each idea to its AWS name.
hint: Use the first column of the translation table.

prompt: Match each product to the provider that sells it.
hint: Two of them come from the smaller providers.

prompt: A team moves an application from RDS for PostgreSQL to Azure. Reading a translation table, they provision Azure SQL Database. What went wrong?
hint: Which engine does each product run?

choices.text: Nothing: the two are the same product under two names
choices.why: The row is the same idea; the engines differ.

choices.text: Azure has no managed PostgreSQL service at all
choices.why: It has one, under its own name: Azure Database for PostgreSQL.

choices.text: That product is SQL Server; the engine changed
choices.why: Right. The table cell holds only if the engine is SQL Server, which is where migrations hurt.

choices.text: RDS data is not allowed to leave AWS for another provider
choices.why: Data leaves at a price per GB; nothing forbids it.

prompt: Why is identity one product at AWS and two at Azure?
hint: Who you are, and what you may do.

choices.text: Entra ID holds the identities; Azure RBAC grants the roles
choices.why: Right. AWS IAM says both things for AWS resources; Azure splits them.

choices.text: Azure has no access control of its own, only a directory
choices.why: Azure RBAC is exactly its access control.

choices.text: AWS has no users at all, only roles that people take on
choices.why: AWS IAM holds users, groups and roles; lesson 7 covers them.

choices.text: They are the same product; the table names it twice by mistake
choices.why: The table names two products in Azure's cell because they do two jobs.

prompt: Google's functions product, called Cloud Functions until 2024, is now Cloud ___ functions.
hint: It is part of the service for running containers.

prompt: The sheet prices m7i.large at 0.16065 USD an hour in sa-east-1 and 0.10080 in us-east-1. How many times the Virginia price is the São Paulo price? Two decimal places.
hint: Divide São Paulo by Virginia.

prompt: In the same capture, t3.medium is 0.06720 USD an hour in sa-east-1 and 0.04160 in us-east-1. What is the São Paulo price as a multiple of Virginia's? Two decimal places.
hint: Same method as m7i.large, another line.

prompt: Put the files in the order you follow them from AWS's price index to a price.
hint: Service, then version, then region.
items: One published version of the offer
One region's file, with products and terms
trap: Region before version is the usual slip: each version is split by region, not the other way round.

prompt: Why does the course's prices.py read a pinned offer version rather than the current one?
hint: What happens to current when AWS publishes?

choices.text: The current version needs an account to download
choices.why: Every version is public; none needs an account.

choices.text: Pinned versions carry cheaper prices than current ones
choices.why: A version records prices; reading an old one changes nothing you pay.

choices.text: Current moves; a price must name its version
choices.why: Right. A pinned sheet prints the same numbers next year and says where they came from.

choices.text: The current file is too large to download every time
choices.why: Size is the same either way; the EC2 file is large at every version.

prompt: You multiply an EC2 machine's hourly price by 730 and the month's bill still comes out higher. Nobody negotiated anything. Where is the difference?
hint: A machine arrives with more than itself.

choices.text: A price list is wrong by design
choices.why: The line was right; it is one line of several.

choices.text: The hourly price rises during the month
choices.why: A version's prices hold still; the list does not move under a running machine.

choices.text: Tax, and nothing else
choices.why: Tax is excluded from the sheet, but the machine's own lines come first.

choices.text: The disk, the public address and data out are lines of their own
choices.why: Right. The machine line is the largest and never the only one; lesson 10 reads the whole bill.

prompt: A Brazilian team wants the short list and a monthly price per machine, and its lawyer says the data has to stay in Brazil. Which provider from this lesson fits?
hint: Regions come before price.

choices.text: Hetzner, for its prices
choices.why: Price is not the first question; Hetzner has no region in South America.

choices.text: DigitalOcean, for the simple bill
choices.why: The bill fits, but DigitalOcean has no data centre in South America.

choices.text: None: only a hyperscaler has a São Paulo region
choices.why: Akamai's cloud has one, with the short list and monthly plans.

choices.text: Akamai's cloud, which has a São Paulo region
choices.why: Right. Of the three smaller providers, it is the one in the country.

prompt: At the sheet's 0.1500 USD per GB for data out of sa-east-1 to the internet, what does moving 2,000 GB out in one month cost at list price?
hint: GB times the price per GB.

prompt: Put the checklist's questions in the order this lesson asks them.
hint: The questions that remove the most candidates come first.
items: Which managed services does the design need?
Where are the users, and where may the data live?
What does the team already know?
What shape will the bill take?
trap: Putting the bill first is the habit this checklist exists to break: a provider that lacks the service or the region is out whatever it costs.

prompt: Which of these move between providers with modest effort? Choose all that apply.
hint: Does every provider sell an equivalent?

choices.text: A PostgreSQL database
choices.why: Every provider in this lesson runs PostgreSQL, managed or on a machine.

choices.text: A DynamoDB table design
choices.why: DynamoDB exists only at AWS; leaving means rewriting.

choices.text: Code that talks to the S3 API
choices.why: S3-compatible storage is sold almost everywhere; change the address and key.

choices.text: Queries written for BigQuery
choices.why: BigQuery is Google's alone; the warehouse and its bills move only by being rebuilt.

choices.text: A virtual machine running Linux
choices.why: The most portable thing on the list: every provider sells one.

prompt: A data team wants to run SQL over very large tables and pay for what each query reads, with no servers to size. Which provider's signature product is that?
hint: A data warehouse, serverless.

choices.text: Google Cloud, with BigQuery
choices.why: Right. It is the product Google's reputation for data rests on.

choices.text: Hetzner, with a dedicated server
choices.why: A dedicated server is the opposite: a machine you size and run.

choices.text: DigitalOcean, with App Platform
choices.why: App Platform runs applications from a repository; it is not a warehouse.

choices.text: Cloudflare, with R2
choices.why: R2 stores objects; it runs no SQL over them.

prompt: A student compares a Droplet's monthly price with an EC2 machine's hourly price times 730 and declares DigitalOcean the cheaper by that difference. What is the mistake?
hint: Step 4 of the method.

choices.text: 730 is the wrong number of hours
choices.why: 24 × 365 / 12 is 730; the arithmetic is fine.

choices.text: None: the machine line is the whole comparison
choices.why: The machine line is one of several at a hyperscaler.

choices.text: Prices in dollars cannot be compared
choices.why: Both are in dollars; the units match.

choices.text: The Droplet's price includes disk, address and transfer that EC2 bills apart
choices.why: Right. Compare the total for what the application needs; the gap is larger than the machine line.

prompt: Match each fact to the provider it belongs to.
hint: One fact per provider; one provider is left over.

pairs.left: A VPC network that is global
Resource groups that delete what they hold
An auction of used dedicated servers

prompt: At every hyperscaler, data coming in from the internet is free and data going ___ is charged per GB.
hint: The opposite of in.

prompt: An AWS bill in dollars is identical two months running, yet a Brazilian company paid a different amount in reais each month. Why?
hint: What converts one into the other?

choices.text: AWS raised its prices in between
choices.why: The bill in dollars was identical, so the list did not move.

choices.text: The exchange rate moved between the two months
choices.why: Right. It is the argument for a provider that bills in reais.

choices.text: Data coming in was charged
choices.why: Data in is 0.0000 on the sheet, and the dollar bill did not change anyway.

choices.text: sa-east-1 bills in reais
choices.why: The sheet prices sa-east-1 in US dollars, like every region.
